contracts.web: src/core/pulsarPanHold.ts: press = one immediate tick, then a 100 ms browser interval of pulsarPanTick using the stored step; a press while held keeps the single running timer. WEB lifecycle: stops on primary pointer up, pointer cancel, capture loss, window blur, page hidden, inactive host, committed load, modal open (tick refused) and unmount; the click that follows a pointer press does not step again. Keyboard/assistive activation (Enter/Space) steps once per physical press: auto-repeated keydowns are ignored and no timer starts; held keys are forgotten on window blur, a hidden page, an inactive host, a load and a modal, because their keyup may never reach the button; the native buttons cannot be keyboard-panned. A tick whose redraw Number cannot represent is refused ('display-unsupported'), which stops the hold. Browser interval cadence vs Windows WM_TIMER resolution/coalescing is not claimed equal. |window| ≤ 1e12 s.

contracts.web: Number, not x87 Extended: an admitted tiny nonzero gain (for example 1e-320) can make the quotient overflow to ±Infinity where Extended stays finite. Such a placement is refused with a visible 'number-unsupported' status; the previous cursor, readout and measurement and the loaded bytes are kept, and a fully refused gesture creates no pending entry;an accepted earlier placement in that gesture stays recordable after a refused MouseUp (WEB Number-domain policy). A later accepted placement replaces the refusal status. No zero substitution, no lower gain limit and no reordered arithmetic is introduced.

contracts.observed: Called after the panel's axis/trace repaint. For each stored time not below Single 0x56c440 (vertical +0xc, reference +0x16; jb skips at 0x56c374/0x56c3b7): x = Round((t − start)·zoom/dt), then 0x56c448 recomputes t from x (re-quantization) and draws only when x ≥ 0. Horizontal value +0x20 not below 0x56c440 (jb 0x56c3fa): y = Round(base[ch] − v·100·gain·factor), then 0x56c6dc without recomputing the value; it draws and stores only for 0 ≤ y < base[ch]. A skipped or rejected cursor is not drawn on the repainted panel, and its stored pixel, value and readout are not rewritten.
contracts.staticData: Single 0x56c440 decodes directly to 0.0 (coordinator static data decode, COORDINATOR-correction-triage/static-data-decode.json). Static evidence only: it does not establish runtime FPU comparison or rounding parity
contracts.web: Each panel cursor carries verticalVisible/referenceVisible/horizontalVisible. A placement sets it (x ≥ 0, or an accepted y), so a negative time or value is drawn right after a manual click. A redraw that skips the entry or rejects its y clears it, keeping the stored pixel, time/value, readout and measurement; a later redraw with a valid projection draws it again. A vertical or reference line is drawn only on a client pixel 0 ≤ x < 400. Keyboard arrows step from a line drawn there; otherwise they use a fixed web edge origin (pixel 0, or row base − 1 for the horizontal cursor). WEB Number boundary: a projection that is not finite in Number (for example v·100 overflowing before gain and factor bring it back, where Extended would not overflow) is not attributed to the native out-of-range rejection. The whole zoom, pan, pan tick or factor change is refused with 'display-unsupported' and changes nothing: no partial re-quantization, no hidden line, the same display, cursors and measurement. The arithmetic order is kept; no gain floor or zero is introduced, and no x87 equivalence is claimed.

contracts.observed: MouseDown: left sets drag flag 0x5dd and places the own cursor by mode 0x57c+ch (0 vertical, 1 horizontal); right sets 0x5dc and places the reference cursor on all three panels. MouseMove acts only with ssLeft (0x08) / ssRight (0x10) while the matching flag is set. MouseUp: clears the flag after the final placement, then 0x57f+ch := IsEmpty || highest < ch; when that is false, Record (+0x464) is enabled.
contracts.web: x,y are clamped to integer client pixels [0,399]×[0,Height[ch]−1]; the native code can receive captured coordinates outside the panel. A WEB toggle maps the primary button/touch to the reference cursor; keyboard arrows act as one click per press. WEB boundary: pointer cancel, lost pointer capture and host deactivation clear both drag latches (pulsarPointerRelease). This is not a native MouseUp: no cursor is placed and no panel becomes pending; cursors, measurement and confirmed list are kept. WEB pointer ownership: only the primary pointer whose press set a latch drives the shared latches; non-primary pointers and other pointers' cancel or capture loss are ignored, so a secondary cancellation does not end the primary drag. Native left/right handling is unchanged and no multi-touch behavior is modelled. WEB Number boundary: a MouseUp whose own placement is refused ('number-unsupported') marks the panel pending only if the same gesture previously stored an accepted placement;otherwise it preserves pending/Record and creates no blank entry. Confirming a record for panel ch forgets ch's accepted placement while the drag latches stay held, so a later refused MouseUp does not make the recorded value pending again. This extra gesture bookkeeping is WEB,not native x87; a y rejected by 0x56c6dc is the native rule and still marks the panel pending

contracts.inference: nativeLineCandidate follows the decoded literals but is not a file-writer contract: the CSV writer is gated and number text is not x87 parity. It is an opaque internal candidate, not a validatable or exportable CSV: the object and file names are wrapped in '"' without escaping, so an admitted name containing an unescaped '"' can make field boundaries ambiguous; a comma within a fully quoted field alone is not evidence of ambiguity. Nothing reads it; Review shows the structured fields, which keep the names verbatim. Native escaping is unknown and is not invented
contracts.web: Comments: printable ASCII without '"', ≤ 80 characters (compiled Cmnt1Ed.MaxLength; the native shortstring storage capacity81 is distinct). The list lives only in this tab; a visible note says it is not part of Save investigation and is discarded on refresh/close. The record and clear prompts are native <dialog> elements opened with showModal() (browser top layer: inert page, contained focus, topmost modal wins); Tab/Shift+Tab wrap via a keydown handler on the dialog element only, never a page-level trap. Escape is Cancel/No, the default button is Cancel/No and focus returns to Record or Clear. A dialog opens only while the panel is active and rendered and no other native modal is open (nonmodal show/open banners do not block it); a bounded observer while a modal session is pending detects conditional DOM removal without close, and local Tab wrapping covers clicks on dialog text; an inactive panel closes it and keeps the record session (draft included) or clear stage for reentry. This is web behavior, not VCL modal parity

contracts.web: src/core/pulsarReviewEdit.ts. pulsarEditorParse/pulsarEditorRebuild are literal models of 0x570498/0x5710d0 over ports of the bound RTL helpers on byte strings. pulsarReviewEditSupport admits an entry only when its nativeLineCandidate and structured fields are printable ASCII 0x20..0x7e (one byte per character), the object has no '"', every structured field and the computed tail fit their ShortString capacities by actual byte length, the candidate equals the structured-field template, the literal parse yields every structured field (a cleared field ↔ null) and the literal rebuild of the parse is byte-identical to the candidate. Other rows are refused with a reason ('text', 'object-quote', 'length' with field/length/capacity, 'layout') and nothing changes; Load and Record admission are unchanged. Commas in the quoted object or comment and quotes or commas inside the file name (opaque tail) are allowed. OK splices the new comment between the raw prefix and suffix and uses the result only when it equals both the literal rebuild and the template; it replaces only the captured working-copy ordinal with a new frozen entry (same sequence, panel and other field strings); other rows keep their identity; an unchanged comment keeps the entry object. The comment is validated by pulsarCommentValid (≤ 80 printable ASCII, no '"'); an invalid draft stays visible in the editor. The confirmed list, measurement comments, pending flags, cursors, readouts, nextSequence, listSaved and saveEnabled change only through the existing outer Ok. The no-selection notice is an inline alertdialog; the editor is an inline layer of the same Review dialog (caption 'Measurement Data', group = object, JD/frequency/gain text, read-only readings out of the Tab order, comment input, OK/Cancel); Enter in the comment is OK; Escape cancels one layer at a time (editor, then Review); focus moves to the comment on open and back to Edit on close; every other Review action is refused while the editor or a notice is open; host inactivity keeps the editor and its draft.
contracts.uncertainty: Static evidence only, not original-equivalent. TMeasForm2 has no own TPF0 resource; inheriting the TMEASFORM DFM and binding OnActivate/OkBtnClick by name to the TMeasForm2 methods and CnclBtnClick to 0x570b30 is the Delphi streaming expectation, not a runtime witness. Review's OnActivate 0x563464 (Items.Assign from the shared list, ItemIndex := 0) may re-run when the nested VCL form closes, before the caller re-reads ItemIndex and Puts; then the original would drop staged deletions and edits and overwrite row 0. The supported subset proves agreement of two chosen models with the stored candidate; nativeLineCandidate stays an internal candidate, not a native Record writer or CSV witness (x87 number text, +0x96 file condition and writer caps remain unbound). VCL TEdit/GDI/ANSI code-page behavior and malformed-input RTL paths outside the subset are not claimed.

contracts.web: pulsarReviewOpen copies the confirmed entry objects into a frozen working copy and selects ordinal 0; Cancel drops it; Ok replaces the confirmed list with it. Selection is an ordinal, never a sequence ID. WEB: an empty working copy has selection null (natively ItemIndex := 0 on an empty list box is expected to read back −1, but that getter result is not recovered here). Rows show the structured fields keyed by the stable sequence; the opaque nativeLineCandidate is not shown, parsed, escaped or rewritten. One radio per row stands for the ListBox selection (browser radio-group arrow keys, which wrap; native ListBox keys are not modelled). Find and Edit are disabled. Tab order follows the document (rows, Delete, Ok, Cancel), not the native TabOrder (buttons before the list), and '&' accelerators are not implemented. WEB initial focus: the selected row, else Cancel. The dialog is a native <dialog> opened with showModal() under the existing PLR modal protocol; Escape and a close request are outer Cancel (no native Cancel property exists). Host inactivity closes the dialog and keeps the session (working copy, selection and inner question) for reentry.

numericPolicy: Metadata and samples are IEEE doubles from Number(lexeme). Native metadata is x87 Extended and samples are Double after an Extended parse. Round() = roundNearestEven (src/core/numericPolicy.ts), not a measured x87 control word. No x87 parity is claimed. A cursor value or record field that is not finite in Number is refused ('number-unsupported'), never stored, formatted as blank or recorded, and a fully refused gesture marks nothing pending. A refused MouseUp preserves recordability of an earlier accepted placement within that same gesture (explicit WEB Number-domain policy). A redraw projection that is not finite in Number refuses the whole display change ('display-unsupported') instead of hiding the line. Operation order is never rearranged to avoid an overflow.

units.time: seconds from the start of the data; sample i is at i·dt
